metadata.description: Pre-compressed reference outputs for round-trip validation and bit-identical comparison
metadata.note: Hex values represent actual compressed output from reference C zlib for the given input, level, and strategy. The Rust implementation must produce byte-identical output for these inputs.
metadata.encoding: Hex bytes are space-separated lowercase, representing the complete compressed stream including headers and trailers where applicable
metadata.generated_with: deflateInit2() + deflate(Z_FINISH) single-pass compression on each input

constants.description: zlib constant values from zlib.h for reference in test code

configuration_table.description: From deflate.c lines 112-124: configuration_table[10] maps compression levels to (good_length, max_lazy, nice_length, max_chain, function). These parameters control the LZ77 matching behavior at each compression level.
configuration_table.note: For deflate_fast (levels 1-3), good_length is ignored and max_lazy has a different meaning (max_insert_length). The deflate code requires max_lazy >= MIN_MATCH (3) and max_chain >= 4.

0.description: Store only — no compression, data is wrapped in stored DEFLATE blocks

2.description: Fast compression with slightly deeper search than level 1

3.description: Fast compression with moderate chain search

4.description: First level to use lazy matching (deflate_slow)

5.description: Balanced speed and compression with lazy matching

6.description: Default compression level — good balance of speed and ratio (Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION maps to 6)

7.description: Higher compression with deeper lazy search

8.description: Near-maximum compression with extensive chain search

9.description: Maximum compression — deepest possible chain search (Z_BEST_COMPRESSION)

compression_levels.description: Reference compressed outputs for 'hello, hello!\0' (14 bytes including null terminator) at each compression level 0-9, using Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY, zlib format (windowBits=15), and default memLevel=8.
compression_levels.input_note: 14 bytes: 13 characters of 'hello, hello!' plus one null terminator byte (0x00), matching test/example.c line 35: static z_const char hello[] = "hello, hello!";
compression_levels.zlib_header_note: The zlib header consists of CMF (0x78 for windowBits=15, deflate method) and FLG which encodes FLEVEL (compression level category): 0x01=level 0-1, 0x5e=level 2-5, 0x9c=level 6, 0xda=level 7-9

vectors.description: No compression — stored blocks, output larger than input
vectors.note: Level 0 uses deflate_stored: zlib header (78 01) + stored block header (01=final, 0e 00=len, f1 ff=~len) + literal data + Adler-32 trailer (26 06 04 96)
FLG=0x01 indicates FLEVEL=0 (fastest algorithm). Compressed DEFLATE block matches 'hello' at distance 7.
FLG=0x5e indicates FLEVEL=1 (fast algorithm). Same DEFLATE payload as level 1 for this small input.
FLG=0x5e indicates FLEVEL=1. Identical output to level 2 for this small input.

vectors.description: First lazy matching level using deflate_slow
vectors.note: FLG=0x5e indicates FLEVEL=1. Despite using deflate_slow, output is identical to levels 2-3 for this small input.
FLG=0x5e indicates FLEVEL=1. Same compressed output as levels 2-4 for this input size.

vectors.description: Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION — default level, balanced speed/ratio using deflate_slow
vectors.note: FLG=0x9c indicates FLEVEL=2 (default algorithm). Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION (-1) maps to level 6 internally.
FLG=0xda indicates FLEVEL=3 (maximum compression algorithm). Same DEFLATE payload for this small input.
FLG=0xda indicates FLEVEL=3. Identical to level 7 output for this input size.

vectors.description: Z_BEST_COMPRESSION — maximum compression using deflate_slow with deepest chain search
vectors.note: FLG=0xda indicates FLEVEL=3. For this small 14-byte input, the compressed payload is identical across all non-stored levels.

strategies.description: Reference compressed outputs showing the effect of different compression strategies on the same input, all at compression level 6 with zlib format (windowBits=15).

vectors.description: Standard LZ77 string matching + dynamic Huffman coding
More Huffman coding, less string matching — best for filtered/predicted data. Produces slightly larger output because it favors shorter matches.
No LZ77 string matching, pure Huffman entropy coding only — no distance codes emitted. FLG changes to 0x01 because the effective compression level is minimal.
vectors.note: Despite level=6, HUFFMAN_ONLY forces FLG to indicate minimal compression (0x01) since no LZ77 matching is performed.

vectors.description: Run-length encoding — match distances limited to 1 byte. Effective only for data with long runs of identical bytes.
vectors.note: RLE strategy produces FLG=0x01. For 'hello, hello!' there are no adjacent repeated bytes, so RLE offers no benefit over HUFFMAN_ONLY.

vectors.description: Uses fixed (pre-defined) Huffman tables instead of dynamic trees. Avoids the overhead of transmitting a custom Huffman tree.
vectors.note: Z_FIXED forces FLG=0x01. For this small input, fixed Huffman matches the compressed size of dynamic Huffman.

formats.description: Same input compressed with different container formats via the windowBits parameter overloading in deflateInit2().

window_bits_encoding.raw_deflate: windowBits = -8..-15 (negative) — RFC 1951 raw DEFLATE, no wrapper
window_bits_encoding.auto_detect: windowBits = 40..47 (32 + 8..15) — inflate auto-detects zlib or gzip

vectors.description: RFC 1950 — 2-byte CMF/FLG header + DEFLATE compressed data + 4-byte Adler-32 trailer
RFC 1951 — Raw DEFLATE stream with no header or trailer. This is the bare compressed data.
RFC 1952 — 10-byte gzip header + DEFLATE compressed data + 4-byte CRC-32 + 4-byte ISIZE trailer

window_sizes.description: Compression with different window sizes (windowBits 9-15) showing how the zlib header CMF byte encodes the window size. All use level 6, Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY, zlib format.
window_sizes.cmf_encoding_note: The CMF byte encodes: CINFO (high nibble) = windowBits - 8, CM (low nibble) = 8 (deflate). So windowBits=9 gives CMF=0x18, windowBits=15 gives CMF=0x78.

round_trip_patterns.description: Various data patterns for round-trip testing (compress then decompress), each with reference compressed output at level 6, Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY, zlib format (windowBits=15). Tests verify that compress→decompress recovers the original input exactly.

vectors.name: empty
vectors.description: Empty input — produces a valid minimal zlib stream with an empty DEFLATE block. The Adler-32 of empty data is 0x00000001 (initial value).

vectors.name: repeated_byte
vectors.description: 16 zero bytes — highly compressible via LZ77 length-distance coding. Demonstrates good compression ratio (16→11 bytes including zlib wrapper, 5 bytes raw DEFLATE).

vectors.name: sequential
vectors.description: Sequential bytes 0x00-0x0F — moderate compressibility. No LZ77 matches possible (all unique bytes), so only Huffman coding applies. Output is larger than input due to Huffman tree overhead for this small input.

vectors.name: all_ff
vectors.input_hex: ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff
vectors.description: 16 bytes of 0xFF — tests all-ones byte pattern. Compressible via LZ77 (repeated byte).

vectors.name: hello_hello
vectors.description: The canonical zlib test string 'hello, hello!' with null terminator — from test/example.c line 35. The repeated 'hello' substring demonstrates LZ77 back-reference matching.

one_call_compress.description: Reference output from the compress() one-call API (compress.c), which uses Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION (level 6 internally), windowBits=15, memLevel=8, Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY.
one_call_compress.note: Output is identical to level 6 with Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY since compress() calls deflateInit with Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION which maps to level 6.

deflate_bound_tests.description: Reference values for deflateBound() — returns the maximum size that deflate() could produce for the given source length. Generated using deflateInit(Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION) + deflateBound(). The actual compressed output must never exceed this value.
deflate_bound_tests.method_note: deflateBound is computed as: sourceLen + (sourceLen >> 12) + (sourceLen >> 14) + (sourceLen >> 25) + 13 (from compress.c compressBound_z). When called via the z_stream API, additional factors for window size and wrapping format may apply.

vectors.description: Empty input bound — minimum overhead is 13 bytes (zlib header + empty deflate block + adler-32)

zlib_header_reference.description: Reference for zlib header byte encoding (RFC 1950 Section 2.2). The zlib header is 2 bytes: CMF and FLG.

cmf_encoding.bits_4_7: CINFO — For CM=8, log2(window_size) - 8. windowBits=15 gives CINFO=7, so CMF = (7 << 4) | 8 = 0x78

flg_encoding.bits_0_4: FCHECK — Check bits so that (CMF * 256 + FLG) is a multiple of 31
flg_encoding.bit_5: FDICT — Set if a preset dictionary is used
